Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarize(total_incidents=n()) %>% 
  slice_max(total_incidents,n = 5)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   county        total_incidents
##   <chr>                   <int>
## 1 San Diego                  25
## 2 Humboldt                   20
## 3 San Mateo                  19
## 4 Santa Barbara              19
## 5 Marin                      16
## 6 Monterey                   16
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  summarize(total_incidents=n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county,y=total_incidents)) +
  geom_col()+
  coord_flip()

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  group_by(month) %>% 
  summarize(total_incidents = n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=month,y=total_incidents)) +
  geom_col()

sharks %>% 
  group_by(month) %>% 
  summarize(total_incidents=n()) %>% 
  slice_max(total_incidents,n=1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   month total_incidents
##   <dbl>           <int>
## 1    10              36
#the month 10 is highest
  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  group_by(time) %>% 
  summarize(total_incidents = n()) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=time,y=total_incidents)) +
  geom_col()+
  coord_flip()

sharks %>% 
  group_by(time) %>% 
  summarize(total_incidents =n()) %>% 
  slice_max(total_incidents,n=1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   time  total_incidents
##   <chr>           <int>
## 1 <NA>               24
#NA time has the highest
  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
injury_count_by_county <- sharks %>% 
  count(county, injury) %>%   
  pivot_wider(names_from=injury,  
              values_from=n, 
              values_fill=0)

injury_count_by_county
## # A tibble: 22 × 8
##    county                 minor  none major `minor*` `none*` fatal `major*`
##    <chr>                  <int> <int> <int>    <int>   <int> <int>    <int>
##  1 Del Norte                  2     1     0        0       0     0        0
##  2 Humboldt                   2     9     7        1       1     0        0
##  3 Island - Catalina          1     3     0        0       0     0        0
##  4 Island - Farallones        0     0     7        0       0     0        0
##  5 Island - San Miguel        2     0     2        0       0     1        0
##  6 Island - San Nicolas       1     0     0        0       0     0        0
##  7 Island - Santa Barbara     0     0     0        0       0     0        1
##  8 Island - Santa Cruz        1     1     0        0       0     0        0
##  9 Island - Santa Rosa        0     0     1        0       0     0        0
## 10 Los Angeles                6     2     0        0       0     1        1
## # ℹ 12 more rows
injury_count_by_county %>% 
  mutate(total_incidents = minor + none + major + `minor*` + `none*`+ fatal + `major*`) %>%  
  slice_max(total_incidents,n=1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 9
##   county    minor  none major `minor*` `none*` fatal `major*` total_incidents
##   <chr>     <int> <int> <int>    <int>   <int> <int>    <int>           <int>
## 1 San Diego     8     9     4        1       1     2        0              25
#san diego is highesst number of incidents
  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
injury_count_by_county %>% 
  mutate(total_incidents = minor + none + major + `minor*` + `none*` + fatal + `major*`) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = county, y = total_incidents)) +
  geom_col()+
  coord_flip()

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  count(mode) %>% 
  slice_max(n, n = 1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   mode                   n
##   <chr>              <int>
## 1 Surfing / Boarding    85
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mode)) +
  geom_bar() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title ="number of incidents by activity",x = "Mode",y = "Number of Incidents")

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
names(sharks)
##  [1] "incident_num"     "month"            "day"              "year"            
##  [5] "time"             "county"           "location"         "mode"            
##  [9] "injury"           "depth"            "species"          "comment"         
## [13] "longitude"        "latitude"         "confirmed_source" "wfl_case_number"
sharks %>% 
  count(species) %>% 
  slice_max(n,n=1)
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   species     n
##   <chr>   <int>
## 1 White     181
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks
## # A tibble: 211 × 16
##    incident_num month   day  year time  county       location mode  injury depth
##           <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <chr> <chr>        <chr>    <chr> <chr>  <chr>
##  1            1    10     8  1950 12:00 San Diego    Imperia… Swim… major  surf…
##  2            2     5    27  1952 14:00 San Diego    Imperia… Swim… minor  surf…
##  3            3    12     7  1952 14:00 Monterey     Lovers … Swim… fatal  surf…
##  4            4     2     6  1955 12:00 Monterey     Pacific… Free… minor  surf…
##  5            5     8    14  1956 16:30 San Luis Ob… Pismo B… Swim… major  surf…
##  6            6     4    28  1957 13:30 San Luis Ob… Morro B… Swim… fatal  surf…
##  7            7    10    12  1958 <NA>  San Diego    Coronad… Swim… major  surf…
##  8            8     5     7  1959 17:30 San Francis… Baker B… Swim… fatal  surf…
##  9            9     6    14  1959 17:00 San Diego    La Jolla Free… fatal  surf…
## 10           10     7    28  1959 19:30 San Diego    La Jolla Free… minor  surf…
## # ℹ 201 more rows
## # ℹ 6 more variables: species <chr>, comment <chr>, longitude <chr>,
## #   latitude <dbl>, confirmed_source <chr>, wfl_case_number <chr>
sharks %>% 
  filter(species=="White") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=injury,fill = injury)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title ="number and types of incidents for Great White's",x = "Injury Type",y = "Number of Incidents")
